correctness.rationale: The geometric classification, explicit coordinates, Frobenius actions, counts and zeta factors check out, but the claim that the incidence scheme itself is finite étale with no scheme multiplicity does not hold for the natural incidence of a bitangent line with a tangent point. At the rational bitangent z=x+y in the chart y=1 the incidence fiber in the curve has equation (x^2+x+1)^2=0. On this line all three homogeneous partial derivatives restrict to the same polynomial x^3+x+1; that polynomial is a unit at either contact (it evaluates to x). The equations for the Gauss tangent to equal this line thus impose no additional local equations. Over the algebraic closure the fiber has two length-two local rings, not two reduced points. Separability of the parameter w^2+w+1 only proves that the reduced flag scheme is finite étale; a bijection on geometric points does not prove the asserted scheme isomorphism. With the reduced structure, the t-chart equations u=t^3, t^7=1 are separable, the two contacts on L_1 are [w:1:w^2], and diagonal rescaling sends these to the stated P_(t,w). Frobenius acts by (t,w)↦(t^2,w^2). The pair-intersection formulas solve two line equations; at x=1 the incidences in t are governed by the monic cubic t^3+yt+z, which precludes more than three lines through a vertex. A triple vertex cannot lie on the smooth quartic, since any such line through it would have to be its unique tangent. The frozen field verifier was inspected rather than run; it checks finite-field points, not incidence local rings.
residual_risks: If Flag is defined as the reduced scheme of geometric flags or via the reduced half-divisor, its étaleness and the displayed arithmetic are correct; this is not the scheme-theoretic assertion for ordinary incidence.
